newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico's PAN picks ex-leader in race for capital.
newsitem.headline: Mexico's PAN picks ex-leader in race for capital.

text.p: Mexico's main opposition force, the centre-right National Action Party (PAN), on Sunday selected ex-leader Carlos Castillo Peraza to run as its candidate in the first election for mayor of Mexico City.

On July 6, residents of the capital, one of the world's largest cities, will elect their ruler, ending a tradition in which the president hand-picked a so-called "regent" from his ruling Institutional Revolutionary Party (PRI).
Mexico's opposition has staked much on winning the capital, seeing it as a major step toward ending the PRI's 68-year grip on power in Mexico.
Opinion polls predicted the opposition was likely to win in the capital, provided they fielded strong candidates.

Castillo, a prickly but popular PAN heavyweight who stepped down as party leader last year, won almost 75 percent of the vote in an internal PAN ballot on Sunday, crushing his main rival. He vowed to take the party to victory.
Mexico City "is the jugular," Vicente Fox, PAN governor of the central state of Guanajuato, said after the vote.
Castillo's main challengers on July 6 will be the PRI's Alfredo del Mazo and a candidate selected Sunday's in the leftist Party of the Democratic Revolution (PRD).
Some 40,000 PRD supporters voted on Sunday to choose between the party's two-time presidential candidate and founder, Cuauhtemoc Cardenas, and its ex-leader Porfirio Munoz Ledo.
Results of that internal ballot were not expected until late on Sunday.
